reason: Round 2: three agents on the routes Kimi K3.1 Pro chose (logistic, l1, knn; oversight/round-2.json), the only open ones, at once, in the sandbox and under the file trace (live/synth-r2-*). All three finished inside the 40-minute wall clock; every trail checks, and each opened the held-out file once, in its final run. Every agent read the map through project_map and built on the pairs route's pilot-only result (logistic on pairwise products, cv 0.8923): the signal is in an interaction, and each agent found a way to reach it. knn is credited: k-nearest neighbours on the raw features and their pairwise products, with an F screen of 10 and k 81 chosen inside cross-validation (cv 0.8568 at step-9, holdout_auc 0.8405 at step-13); its route allows any feature screen chosen inside cross-validation. l1 is credited: an L1-penalised logistic regression on the raw features and their pairwise products, C tuned inside cross-validation (cv 0.9134 at step-11, holdout_auc 0.9079 at step-22); its route names the penalty and the tuning, not the features. logistic is not credited, by judgment: its route is a logistic regression on the features as given, and the agent's own pilot diagnostics showed that capped at 0.63 (its steps 6-7). It moved to an RBF-kernel logistic regression (cv 0.8678 at step-19, holdout_auc 0.8667 at step-22), a different method. The two candidates are declined, logistic-cv and logistic-holdout stay open, and the forecasts of them stay unsettled. A later revision, or a person, can reverse this. The routes were chosen in spec 12 to sit far below, near and far above the floor by their default methods; tuned agents that read each other's results put all of them above it. The round 2 credits rest, through what the agents built on, on round 1's two row counts (forest step-4, pairs step-4), excused as in rev-1.
